The kth segment can cross each of the k−1 earlier segments at most once. Those crossings divide the new segment into at most k pieces. Each piece can split one existing section, so the kth segment adds at most k sections.
This bound is attainable: draw the three new segments through a common interior point of MN at different angles, then shift them slightly so all pairwise crossings remain inside the rectangle but no three coincide. Each new segment then passes through a different section between successive crossings, since it never crosses an earlier segment twice.
Starting with one section, the maximum is 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 11.
Final answer: 11
